speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to begin our assessment, how long has this rash been present and does the itching occur continuously or only in response to heat, sweating, or contact with specific materials?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash has persisted for five months without complete resolution. Have you noticed any specific pattern, such as the rash appearing or worsening after warm showers, or have you recently used any new skincare products like lotions or detergents?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies. The 5-month duration, bilateral upper extremity involvement, and worsening with warmth (sweat) are classic indicators of this parasitic infestation.
